market_question: Will the Republicans win the 2028 US Presidential Election?
reasoning: The market implies only 38.5% for Republicans, but a one-term Trump presidency (non-consecutive) ending in 2029 creates an open-seat election without the usual 8-year fatigue. Historical open-seat races after a single party term + incumbency advantages suggest Republicans have a better chance than the market believes, though uncertainty remains high this far out.
evidence_points: Trump cannot run again, but the Republican incumbency will be only one term (2025-2029), not two consecutive, reducing voter fatigue.

Historical open-seat elections after one-term or two-term presidencies show the incumbent party winning roughly 35-50% of the time, with the most analogous cases (open seat after 8-year two-term) slightly favoring the opposition but not as low as 38.5%.

Early polls and betting markets for 2028 show Democrats as marginal favorites but not overwhelming; the current 61.5% Democratic probability appears too high given party polarization and the inherent uncertainty 4 years ahead.
